claim: The syncytiotrophoblast (STB) is a multinucleated cell layer that forms the outer surface of human chorionic villi.
source: The syncytiotrophoblast (STB) is a multinucleated cell layer that forms the outer surface of human chorionic villi.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established scientific knowledge about placental structure.

claim: The STB contains billions of nuclei in a single cell.
source: Its unusual structure, with billions of nuclei in a single cell, makes it difficult to resolve using conventional single-cell methods.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Barker et al., 1973; Burton and Jauniaux, 1995; Haeussner et al., 2014).

claim: Single-nucleus RNA-seq is essential for capturing STB populations.
source: Single-nucleus RNA-seq was essential for capturing STB populations, revealing three nuclear subtypes: a juvenile subtype co-expressing CTB and STB markers, one enriched in oxygen sensing genes, and another in transport and GTPase signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Three STB nuclear subtypes exist: a juvenile subtype co-expressing CTB and STB markers, one enriched in oxygen sensing genes, and another in transport and GTPase signaling.
source: Single-nucleus RNA-seq was essential for capturing STB populations, revealing three nuclear subtypes: a juvenile subtype co-expressing CTB and STB markers, one enriched in oxygen sensing genes, and another in transport and GTPase signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Organoids grown in suspension culture (STBout) showed higher expression of STB markers and hormones.
source: Organoids grown in suspension culture (STBout) showed higher expression of STB markers, hormones, and a greater proportion of the transport-associated nuclear subtype while TOs grown with an inverted polarity (STBin) exhibited a higher proportion of the oxygen sensing nuclear subtype.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: STBout organoids have a greater proportion of the transport-associated nuclear subtype.
source: Organoids grown in suspension culture (STBout) showed higher expression of STB markers, hormones, and a greater proportion of the transport-associated nuclear subtype while TOs grown with an inverted polarity (STBin) exhibited a higher proportion of the oxygen sensing nuclear subtype.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: STBin organoids exhibited a higher proportion of the oxygen sensing nuclear subtype.
source: Organoids grown in suspension culture (STBout) showed higher expression of STB markers, hormones, and a greater proportion of the transport-associated nuclear subtype while TOs grown with an inverted polarity (STBin) exhibited a higher proportion of the oxygen sensing nuclear subtype.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Gene regulatory analysis identified RYBP as a conserved STB marker.
source: Gene regulatory analysis identified conserved STB markers, including the chromatin remodeler RYBP.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: RYBP knockout did not impair fusion.
source: Although RYBP knockout did not impair fusion, it downregulated CSH1 and upregulated oxygen-sensing genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: RYBP knockout downregulated CSH1.
source: Although RYBP knockout did not impair fusion, it downregulated CSH1 and upregulated oxygen-sensing genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: RYBP knockout upregulated oxygen-sensing genes.
source: Although RYBP knockout did not impair fusion, it downregulated CSH1 and upregulated oxygen-sensing genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: The placenta facilitates molecular exchange, performs essential metabolic functions, produces hormones, prevents loss of immune tolerance, and acts as a barrier against vertical transmission of pathogens.
source: While the fetal organs undergo development, the placenta assumes a multifaceted role, serving to facilitate molecular exchange, perform essential metabolic functions, produce hormones, prevent loss of immune tolerance, and act as a barrier against the vertical transmission of pathogens (Aye et al., 2022; Benirschke et al., 2012; Costa, 2016; Megli and Coyne, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The STB envelops the chorionic villi.
source: Its outer layer encompasses a giant single cell called the syncytiotrophoblast (STB), that contains billions of nuclei and envelops the chorionic villi (Barker et al., 1973; Burton and Jauniaux, 1995; Haeussner et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The STB is formed via cell-cell fusion of the underlying cytotrophoblast (CTB) cell population.
source: The STB is formed via cell-cell fusion of the underlying cytotrophoblast (CTB) cell population.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge about STB formation.

claim: CTBs reside on the basement membrane of chorionic villi to contribute new nuclei into the STB or lie at the interface between the placenta villi and the maternal decidua in multi-cell layered structures termed cell columns (CTB-CC; Figure 1A; Boyd and Hamilton, 1970).
source: CTBs reside on the basement membrane of chorionic villi to contribute new nuclei into the STB or lie at the interface between the placenta villi and the maternal decidua in multi-cell layered structures termed cell columns (CTB-CC; Figure 1A; Boyd and Hamilton, 1970).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: CTBs closer to the maternal decidua are more differentiated than their counterparts lower in the column.
source: CTBs closer to the maternal decidua are more differentiated than their counterparts lower in the column and eventually undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) to form fully differentiated extravillous trophoblast (EVT) cells that invade into the decidua (Figure 1A; Arutyunyan et al., 2023; Turco and Moffett, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: CTBs undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) to form fully differentiated extravillous trophoblast (EVT) cells that invade into the decidua.
source: CTBs closer to the maternal decidua are more differentiated than their counterparts lower in the column and eventually undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) to form fully differentiated extravillous trophoblast (EVT) cells that invade into the decidua (Figure 1A; Arutyunyan et al., 2023; Turco and Moffett, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing has been applied to characterize EVT differentiation in primary tissue, trophoblast organoids, and trophoblast stem cells.
source: Several groups have applied single-cell RNA sequencing (SC) of primary tissue throughout gestation, trophoblast organoids (TOs), and trophoblast stem cells (TSCs) to characterize EVT differentiation (Arutyunyan et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2018; Marsh et al., 2022; Pique-Regi et al., 2019; Shannon et al., 2024; Suryawanshi et al., 2018; Vento-Tormo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Previous single-cell datasets contain very few cells from the STB.
source: However, these datasets contain very few cells from the STB, limiting characterization of the CTB-to-STB differentiation process.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is a key motivation for the study.

claim: The STB is excluded during single-cell isolation and size filtration steps required for the 10x Genomics microfluidics pipeline.
source: This scarcity likely arises because the STB, being a large single cell, is excluded during the single-cell isolation and size filtration steps required for the 10 x Genomics microfluidics pipeline.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference about why STB is underrepresented in single-cell datasets.

claim: A recent study performed single-nucleus sequencing on placenta tissue and captured STB nuclei, defining their lineage trajectories at each gestational age.
source: In fact, a recent study performed SN on placenta tissue (six first trimester and six full-term tissues) and captured STB nuclei and defined their lineage trajectories at each gestational age (Wang et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Wang et al., 2024.

claim: The STB can bifurcate into at least two nuclear lineages post-fusion, associated with either hormone expression and GTPase signaling or with an oxygen response.
source: Their analysis suggests that the STB can bifurcate into at least two nuclear lineages post-fusion, associated with either hormone expression and GTPase signaling or with an oxygen response.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction, citing findings from Wang et al., 2024.

claim: There is remarkable diversity of placental structures amongst mammals.
source: A major challenge in establishing genetically tractable and accessible models for the human placenta is the remarkable diversity of placental structures amongst mammals, and notably the variations in the tissue architecture and cell types seen even between humans and mice (Hemberger et al., 2020; Wooding and Burton, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CTB progenitor cells can be isolated from tissue throughout gestation.
source: CTB progenitor cells can be isolated from tissue throughout gestation, as CTB remain mitotic throughout pregnancy (Haider et al., 2018; Mayhew, 2014; Turco and Moffett, 2019; Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CTB remain mitotic throughout pregnancy.
source: CTB progenitor cells can be isolated from tissue throughout gestation, as CTB remain mitotic throughout pregnancy (Haider et al., 2018; Mayhew, 2014; Turco and Moffett, 2019; Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CTB can be maintained in a proliferative state capable of trophoblast differentiation by using a growth factor cocktail and cultivation in extracellular matrix.
source: They can subsequently be maintained in a proliferative state capable of trophoblast differentiation by using a growth factor cocktail and cultivation in extracellular matrix (Okae et al., 2018; Turco et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2022), and spontaneously fuse to form STB (Haider et al., 2018; Li et al., 2023; Turco and Moffett, 2019; Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CTB spontaneously fuse to form STB in organoid culture.
source: They can subsequently be maintained in a proliferative state capable of trophoblast differentiation by using a growth factor cocktail and cultivation in extracellular matrix (Okae et al., 2018; Turco et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2022), and spontaneously fuse to form STB (Haider et al., 2018; Li et al., 2023; Turco and Moffett, 2019; Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: In standard culture conditions, TOs exhibit an inverted architecture with an outward facing proliferative CTB layer and a largely inward facing STB (STBin).
source: In standard culture conditions, TOs exhibit an inverted architecture compared to placental villi in vivo, with an outward facing proliferative CTB layer and a largely inward facing STB (STBin; Haider et al., 2018; Turco and Moffett, 2019; Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: A method has been established to reverse the cellular polarity of TOs to their native orientation, resulting in organoids with STB on the outermost layer (STBout).
source: Our recent work has established a method to reverse the cellular polarity of TOs to their native orientation, resulting in organoids containing very large (>50 nuclei) STB on the outermost layer and mononuclear CTBs positioned in the center (STBout), and exhibit increased secretion of the STB-associated hormone human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) (Yang et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Yang et al., 2024.

claim: STBout organoids contain very large STB with >50 nuclei.
source: Our recent work has established a method to reverse the cellular polarity of TOs to their native orientation, resulting in organoids containing very large (>50 nuclei) STB on the outermost layer and mononuclear CTBs positioned in the center (STBout), and exhibit increased secretion of the STB-associated hormone human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) (Yang et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Yang et al., 2024.

claim: STBout organoids exhibit increased secretion of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG).
source: Our recent work has established a method to reverse the cellular polarity of TOs to their native orientation, resulting in organoids containing very large (>50 nuclei) STB on the outermost layer and mononuclear CTBs positioned in the center (STBout), and exhibit increased secretion of the STB-associated hormone human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) (Yang et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Yang et al., 2024.

claim: A small proportion of CTBs in TOs can spontaneously differentiate into HLA-G+ EVTs.
source: While the majority of CTBs in TOs differentiate into the STB, a small proportion can spontaneously differentiate into HLA-G+ EVTs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: EVT percentage can be increased through a three-step treatment involving Neuregulin-1 (NRG1).
source: This EVT percentage can be increased through a three-step treatment involving Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) (EVTenrich; Haider et al., 2018; Turco and Moffett, 2019; Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The SC tissue dataset captured only 6% STB of total cells.
source: As in previous single-cell approaches, our SC tissue dataset captured only a small fraction of the STB cell type (6% of total cells are STB).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: The SN tissue dataset captured 76% STB of total nuclei.
source: In contrast, the predominant population in the SN preparation was STB nuclei, accounting for 76% of the total nuclei count, (Figure 1D-E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B) and consistent with their relative prevalence in vivo (Mayhew, 2014; Mayhew and Simpson, 1994; Simpson et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: The SN dataset on primary tissue had an 8:1 ratio of STB to CTB, resembling stereological estimates of placental trophoblast compositions at full-term (9:1).
source: Specifically, the SN dataset on primary tissue had an 8:1 ratio of STB to CTB, resembling stereological estimates of placental trophoblast compositions at full-term (9:1) indicating that enzymatic digestion of nuclei is capturing a representative population of these trophoblast nucleus types. (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1D.

claim: SC sequencing exhibited significant enrichment in EVT (18% of total in SC vs. 1.3% in SN).
source: While the STB subtype is better captured by SN sequencing, SC sequencing exhibited significant enrichment in both EVT (18% of total in SC vs. 1.3% in SN) and macrophages (53% of total in SC vs. 1.9% in SN) (Figure 1D–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: SC sequencing exhibited significant enrichment in macrophages (53% of total in SC vs. 1.9% in SN).
source: While the STB subtype is better captured by SN sequencing, SC sequencing exhibited significant enrichment in both EVT (18% of total in SC vs. 1.3% in SN) and macrophages (53% of total in SC vs. 1.9% in SN) (Figure 1D–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: In TOs, the SC dataset captured only 2.4% of the total STB population.
source: Like placenta tissue, the SC dataset captured only a small number of the total STB present in TOs, with only 2.4% of the total cell population attributed to the STB (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: In TOs, the STB accounted for 38% of the total nuclear numbers captured by SN sequencing.
source: In contrast, the STB accounted for 38% of the total nuclear numbers captured by SN sequencing (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: STB nuclei accounted for 39% in STBin, 53% in STBout, and 4% in EVTenrich of the total population.
source: In each culture condition STB nuclei were present, accounting for 39% (STBin), 53% (STBout), and 4% (EVTenrich) of the total population (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: EVTs accounted for 24% of the total population in EVTenrich TOs.
source: In contrast, EVTs accounted for 24% of the total population in EVTenrich TOs and separated into two clusters (EVT-1, EVT-2) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: The STB:CTB ratio was nearly halved in STBin compared to STBout (1.3:1 in STBin versus 2.5:1 in STBout).
source: Despite CTB-pf accounting for 7% of each dataset in STBin and STBout, the STB:CTB ratio was nearly halved in STBin compared to STBout (1.3:1 in STBin versus 2.5:1 in STBout).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: STB-1 expressed genes previously associated with CTBs, including the TFs TEAD1 and TP63.
source: STB-1 is closest to CTB-pf on the UMAP and expressed many genes previously associated with CTBs, including the TFs TEAD1 and TP63 (Figures 2D and 3B; Li et al., 2014; Mizutani et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and supported by data in Figures 2D and 3B.

claim: STB-2 expressed FLT1, INHBA, and PAPPA2, associating this subtype with ER stress and oxygen sensing.
source: STB-2 expressed a unique subset of genes that included the VEGF receptor FLT1, the TGFβ family member INHBA, and the insulin regulator PAPPA2, associating this subtype with ER stress and oxygen sensing (Figure 3B–C; Barrios et al., 2021; Li et al., 2022; Sasagawa et al., 2021; Sasagawa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and supported by data in Figure 3B-C.

claim: STB-2 was more abundant in STBin than STBout.
source: Interestingly, STB-2 was more abundant in STBin than STBout (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: The percentage of STB-3 nuclei were doubled from 20% in STBin to 40% in STBout.
source: In contrast to STB-1 and STB-2, the percentage of STB-3 nuclei were doubled from 20% in STBin to 40% in STBout.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: Pseudotime analysis revealed a continuous trajectory starting from CTB-p, traversing through CTBs to CTB-pf, and progressing through STB-1 and STB-2 before culminating in the STB-3 subtype.
source: This visualization revealed a continuous trajectory starting from CTB-p subtype, traversing through CTBs to CTB-pf, and progressing through STB-1 and STB-2 before culminating in the STB-3 subtype (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4A.

claim: RYBP and AFF1 were two genes most significantly associated with the CTB to STB pseudotime trajectory and enhanced in STBout TOs.
source: Interestingly, the chromatin remodeler (CR) RYBP and transcriptional activator AFF1 were two genes most significantly associated with the CTB to STB pseudotime trajectory and enhanced in STBout TOs (Figure 4B–C), suggesting they may play roles in initiating transcription of genes involved in STBout nuclear differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4B-C.

claim: RYBP exhibited STB-specific localization in term placenta tissue.
source: We found that RYBP exhibited STB-specific localization in term placenta tissue (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: RYBP exhibited STB specific expression in both STBin and STBout TOs.
source: RYBP exhibited STB specific expression in both STBin and STBout TOs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5B-C.

claim: No difference in the overall morphology of TOs was found in RYBP knockout, and size and number of nuclei within the STB remained constant.
source: No difference in the overall morphology of TOs was found, and size and number of nuclei within the STB remained constant (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5D.

claim: Deletion of either RYBP or AFF1 resulted in significant increased expression of genes associated with the STB-2 oxygen sensing subtype.
source: We found that deletion of either RYBP or AFF1 resulted in significant increased expression of genes associated with the STB-2 oxygen sensing subtype, including FLT1, PAPPA2, SPON2, SFXN3, and many of the PSG hormones involved in angiogenesis (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5E.

claim: CSH1 was significantly upregulated in WT TOs compared to RYBP-/- and AFF1-/- TOs.
source: In contrast, the human placenta lactogen gene (CSH1) was significantly upregulated in WT TOs compared to RYBP-/- and AFF1-/- TOs, suggesting deletion of both RYBP and AFF1 affect the expression of a hormone increased in STBout TOs (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 3, and Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5E.

claim: The proportion of STB:CTB was higher in full-term tissue than in first trimester tissue (7:1 at full-term vs 1.5:1 in first trimester).
source: The proportion of STB:CTB was higher in full-term tissue than in first trimester tissue (7:1 at full-term vs 1.5:1 in first trimester, combined dataset), as anticipated given the higher proportion of CTBs in first trimester (Figure 6B; Benirschke et al., 2012; Mayhew, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: The STB:CTB ratios in TOs more closely resembled first trimester than term tissue in both culture conditions (1:1 for STBout and 0.6:1 for STBin).
source: Of note, the STB:CTB ratios in TOs more closely resembled first trimester than term tissue in both culture conditions (1:1 for STBout and 0.6:1 for STBin; Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: GO terms associated with the CTB populations were remarkably conserved amongst all sample types.
source: GO terms associated with the CTB populations were remarkably conserved amongst all sample types (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: STB exhibited greater diversity of functions between sample types than CTBs.
source: In contrast, STB exhibited greater diversity of functions between sample types (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6E.

claim: STB from first trimester expressed hCG genes while there was no expression in full-term tissue.
source: Consistent with these gestational hormone trends, STB from first trimester expressed hCG genes while there was no expression in full-term tissue (Figure 6G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6G.

claim: Full-term tissue exhibited an increase in CSH1 expression compared to first trimester.
source: Further, full-term tissue exhibited an increase in CSH1 expression compared to first trimester (Figure 6G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6G.

claim: STBin and STBout TOs expressed both hCG and CSH1 hormones in the STB.
source: STBin and STBout TOs expressed both hormones in the STB suggesting organoids can produce hormones differentially expressed throughout gestation (Figure 6G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6G.

claim: There was an increase in the expression of FLT1 and decrease in PAPPA in the STB of first trimester compared to full-term tissue.
source: Consistent with previous reports, there was an increase in the expression of FLT1 and decrease in PAPPA in the STB of first trimester compared to full-term tissue, with TOs resembling first trimester expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G–H; Wang et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G-H.

claim: TOs resemble first trimester expression of FLT1 and PAPPA.
source: Consistent with previous reports, there was an increase in the expression of FLT1 and decrease in PAPPA in the STB of first trimester compared to full-term tissue, with TOs resembling first trimester expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G–H; Wang et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G-H.

claim: STBout culture conditions promotes STB differentiation and prevents CTB-CC differentiation down the EVT lineage.
source: Of note, there was a higher percentage of CTB-3 that expressed CTB-CC markers in STBin (20% of STBin and 11% of STBout) and a decrease in the STB-3 population (9% of STBin and 20% of STBout; Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) suggesting that STBout culture conditions promotes STB differentiation and prevents CTB-CC differentiation down the EVT lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: STBout TOs expressed higher levels of key STB markers and hormones.
source: Similarly, STBout TOs expressed higher levels of key STB markers and hormones, indicating culture in suspension promotes enhanced STB differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: EVTenrich conditions promote CTB differentiation into EVT instead of STB.
source: In particular, STBin TOs had a dramatic increase in STB nucleus types (37% of STBin and 7% of EVTenrich) while EVTenrich exhibited an increase in EVT types (5% of STBin and 30% of EVTenrich; Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), validating EVTenrich conditions promote CTB differentiation into EVT instead of STB.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: Both TO and TSC models showed a nearly equivalent composition of trophoblast nucleus types.
source: Both TO and TSC models showed a nearly equivalent composition of trophoblast nucleus types, including CTB-p, CTB-pf, EVTs, and two distinct STB populations (STB-1 and STB-2; Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-C.

claim: TSC-derived CTB-pf and STB clusters highly expressed the EVT marker HLA-G, which was absent in TO-derived CTB-pf and STBs.
source: TSC-derived CTB-pf and STB clusters highly expressed the EVT marker HLA-G, which was absent in TO-derived CTB-pf and STBs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D.

claim: TO-derived CTB-pf and STBs showed significantly higher expression of STB-associated hormones and other factors, including PSGs, CGBs, CSH1, HOPX, and KISS1.
source: Additionally, TO-derived CTB-pf and STBs showed significantly higher expression of STB-associated hormones and other factors, including PSGs, CGBs, CSH1, HOPX, and KISS1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D–E; Costa, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D-E.

claim: The proportion of mitotic cells remains constant between TOs grown in STBin and STBout conditions.
source: Here we show that the proportion of mitotic cells remains constant between TOs grown in STBin and STBout conditions, suggesting culture in suspension is not a terminal, post-mitotic state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data presented earlier.

claim: The increase of STB in the STBout condition could be caused by promotion of STB lineage and an inhibition of differentiation down a CTB-CC or EVT lineage.
source: Therefore, the increase of STB in the STBout condition could be caused by promotion of STB lineage and an inhibition of differentiation down a CTB-CC or EVT lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.

claim: STB-1 represents a juvenile population undergoing a transition from CTB to STB gene expression.
source: STB-1 represented a juvenile population undergoing a transition from CTB to STB gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: STB-2 might play a role in responding to low oxygen levels.
source: STB-2 expressed the VEGF receptor FLT1 and is enriched in genes involved in responding to oxygen levels and ER stress, suggesting STB-2 might play a role in responding to low oxygen levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: STB-3 is hypothesized to be a terminal differentiation state.
source: We hypothesize the STB-3 subtype is a terminal differentiation state as it appears at the end of the slingshot pseudotime trajectory.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on the pseudotime analysis.

claim: Growth in either extracellular matrix (STBin) or suspension (STBout) impacts both the cell orientation and environmental cues each cell type is exposed to.
source: We hypothesize growth in either extracellular matrix (STBin) or suspension (STBout) impacts both the cell orientation and environmental cues each cell type is exposed to like oxygen concentrations, cell and membrane tension, and media flow dynamics.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: The environmental cues the STB experiences throughout gestation may affect STB subtype distribution in vivo.
source: The distribution of STB subtypes defined in Wang et al., 2024 also changed throughout gestation with the oxygen sensing STB nuclear subtype increased in the first trimester and the GTPase/hormone subtype increased at term and implies the environmental cues the STB experiences throughout gestation may affect STB subtype distribution in vivo similar to what is seen in TOs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference based on comparison with Wang et al., 2024.

claim: Individual nucleus identities might be spatially localized to different cytoplasmic regions in the STB.
source: One potential mechanism for creating these distinct cytoplasmic zones is nuclear specialization, whereby individual nucleus identities might be spatially localized to different cytoplasmic regions, as has been demonstrated for nuclei in syncytial muscle fibers (Kim et al., 2020; Petrany et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis with citations to analogous findings in muscle fibers.

claim: RYBP acts to downregulate the STB-2 nuclear subtype in STBin TOs.
source: To test this idea, we deleted RYBP with CRISPR/Cas9 in TOs and observed an increase in many STB-2 nuclear subtype marker genes and a significant decrease in the human placenta lactogen gene. This suggests that RYBP acts to downregulate the STB-2 nuclear subtype in STBin TOs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the RYBP knockout data.

claim: RYBP deletion in mice is embryonic lethal due in part to a failure to form trophectoderm and subsequent invasion defects.
source: Of note, RYBP deletion in mice is embryonic lethal due in part to a failure to form trophectoderm and subsequent invasion defects (Pirity et al., 2005), consistent with a possible role of RYBP on STB differentiation in human placenta.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to Pirity et al., 2005.

claim: The cues that restrict hormones to different gestational stages in vivo are not intrinsic to the isolated CTBs.
source: We found that while the TOs used in this study were derived from full-term CTBs, the STB associated with these organoids express hormone transcripts classically associated with early gestation. This suggests that the cues that restrict these hormones to different gestational stages in vivo are not intrinsic to the isolated CTBs and can be studied in full-term derived TOs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the hormone expression data.

claim: Environmental cues can direct individual nuclei in the same cell into different identities.
source: The fluctuating proportions of STB subtypes across TO culture conditions imply that environmental cues can direct individual nuclei in the same cell into different identities.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.

claim: Placenta tissue was collected from patients undergoing scheduled C-sections at UNC Health consented under IRB 21–2055.
source: Placenta tissue was collected from patients undergoing scheduled C-sections at UNC Health consented under IRB 21–2055.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing tissue collection procedures.

claim: 10,000 single cells or nuclei of each sample type were loaded into individual chip wells and run on a 10x chromium controller.
source: 10,000 SC/SN of each sample type were loaded into individual chip wells and run on a 10 x chromium controller with the Chromium Single Cell 3' Reagent Reagent Kit v3.1 (Dual Index) following the manufacturers protocol.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the 10X genomics library generation.

claim: Tissue libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq S2 at a targeted sequencing depth of 100,000 reads/cell or nucleus.
source: Tissue libraries were then sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq S2 at a targeted sequencing depth of 100,000 reads/cell or nucleus while organoid libraries were sequenced on an Illumna NovaSeq S4 at a targeted sequencing depth of 74,000 reads/cell or nucleus.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing sequencing procedures.
